The evidence on minimum wage increases

Over the past three decades, a large body of research has examined what happens to workers and businesses when the minimum wage goes up, across states, cities and countries.

Our review finds that minimum wage increases have not caused significant job losses, even as they have raised pay for millions of low-wage workers and narrowed gender and racial pay gaps.

Studies that compare neighboring counties on either side of a state border consistently find small or no employment effects, while studies that find large job losses tend to rely on comparisons between very different places.

Policymakers should consider these findings when debating proposals for a higher federal minimum wage.
